data.narrative:
Brimstone is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Cody Finke and Hugo Leandri that has raised $100M+. The sector comprises 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though a sufficiently narrow peer set at the same stage and valuation tier could not be constructed from available data.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and forms the sole quantitative anchor for this analysis. Using the $100M total raised as a valuation proxy, a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A progression to the next funding stage implies a post-valuation of $200M. This method rests on the assumption that capital deployed approximates pre-money valuation and that step-up velocity aligns with historical medians for the sector. The Peer-Median approach was not applicable: while 9 same-sector comps exist (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen among private peers), none of the narrow filters—same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded three or more datapoints. Broadening to all-sector comps without these controls would introduce material estimation error.

The triangulated range is $170M (low) to $230M (high), with a median of $200M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method and therefore carries elevated sensitivity to the stage-step multiplier assumption. Key uncertainties include the appropriate comparables-based discount or premium relative to raised capital, the actual pre-money valuation at the most recent close, and burn trajectory relative to sector benchmarks.
